(Baltimore, Maryland) *[[Montverde Academy]]
([[Montverde, Florida]]) | college = [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]] (2024–present) | highlights = * First-team All-[[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] ([[2024–25 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|2025]]) * [[Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year|Big Ten Freshman of the Year]] (2025) * Big Ten All-Freshman Team (2025) * [[McDonald's All-American Game]] [[Most valuable player|Co-MVP]] ([[2024 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2024]]) }} '''Derik Queen''' (born December 27, 2004) is an American basketball player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland Terrapins]] of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. He played [[high school basketball]] for [[Montverde Academy]] and was a consensus five-star [[College recruiting|recruit]] in the 2024 class. ==High school career== As a freshman, Queen attended [[Saint Frances Academy (Baltimore)|Saint Frances Academy]] in his native [[Baltimore]].{{cite news |last1=Graham |first1=Glenn |last2=Lee |first2=Edward |name-list-style=and |date=February 21, 2024 |title=Derik Queen, a 5-star recruit from Baltimore, commits to Maryland men’s basketball |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2024/02/21/derik-queen-commits-maryland-mens-basketball/ |access-date=February 24, 2024 |work=[[The Baltimore Sun]]}} On March 12, 2021, he scored a season-high 56 points in a 99–55 win over [[Annapolis Area Christian School]].{{cite news |last=Graham |first=Glenn |date=April 19, 2021 |title=St. Frances basketball star Derik Queen named MaxPreps National Freshman of the Year |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2021/04/19/st-frances-basketball-star-derik-queen-named-maxpreps-national-freshman-of-the-year/ |access-date=February 23, 2024 |work=[[The Baltimore Sun]]}} Queen averaged 14 points, eight rebounds, four assists and two blocks per game during the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-shortened]] season, leading the Panthers to a 15–1 record and an appearance in the [[Baltimore Catholic League]] title game. He was named the [[MaxPreps National Basketball Player of the Year awards#Freshman of the Year|MaxPreps National Freshman of the Year]] for his performance. Following the season, Queen transferred to [[Montverde Academy]] in [[Montverde, Florida]].{{cite news |last=Divens |first=Jordan |date=July 28, 2021 |title=High school basketball: MaxPreps National Freshman of the Year Derik Queen headed to Montverde Academy, giving Eagles 11 top 60 prospects next season |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/-bRmSUiqyE2IrQ5qTGnDUQ/high-school-basketball-maxpreps-national-freshman-of-the-year-derik-queen-headed-to-montverde-academy%2C-giving-eagles-11-top-60-prospects-next-season.htm |access-date=February 23, 2024 |work=[[MaxPreps]]}} He received limited playing time as a sophomore due to the amount of talent on the team, which won its second straight GEICO Nationals title with a 60–49 win over [[Link Academy (Missouri)|Link Academy]].{{cite news |last=Schumann |first=Mike |date=January 9, 2023 |title=Rapidly improving 2024 big man Derik Queen gives thoughts on IU basketball, overall recruitment |url=https://www.thedailyhoosier.com/rapidly-improving-2024-big-man-derik-queen-gives-thoughts-on-iu-basketball-overall-recruitment/ |access-date=February 23, 2024 |work=The Daily Hoosier}}{{cite news |last=Hardwig |first=Greg |date=April 2, 2022 |title=High school basketball: Montverde Academy wins sixth GEICO Nationals boys championship |url=https://www.news-press.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2022/04/02/montverde-academy-wins-sixth-geico-nationals-boys-basketball-championship-fort-myers-link-academy/7199703001/ |access-date=February 23, 2024 |work=[[The News-Press]]}} On December 9, 2022, Queen recorded his first [[double-double]] at Montverde, contributing 11 points and 11 rebounds during a 78–51 win over [[Oak Hill Academy (Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]] at the Bob Kirk Invitational Showcase.{{cite news |title=Derik Queen's Basketball Stats {{!}} Varsity 22-23 |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/fl/montverde/montverde-academy-eagles/athletes/derik-queen/basketball/stats/?careerid=ts8q2t6671sg0&sportSeasonId=77be7c75-cdf9-483d-867f-ea2af557e731#year=22-23 |access-date=February 23, 2024 |publisher=[[MaxPreps]]}}{{cite news |last=Bennett |first=Kyle |date=December 11, 2022 |title=Balanced scoring attack sends Montverde past Oak Hill, 78-51 |url=https://www.times-news.com/sports/local_sports/balanced-scoring-attack-sends-montverde-past-oak-hill-78-51/article_efb2f09e-783e-11ed-afdb-ab9f4200fbbf.html |access-date=February 23, 2024 |work=[[Cumberland Times-News]]}} On December 21, he tallied 13 points and a season-high 16 rebounds in a 79–45 win over [[Milton High School (Georgia)|Milton High School]] at the 'Iolani Classic.{{cite news |date=December 22, 2022 |title=Boys’ Basketball Closes Out ‘Iolani Classic with Win over Milton |url=https://mvasports.com/news/2022/12/22/boys-basketball-boys-basketball-closes-out-iolani-classic-with-win-over-milton.aspx |access-date=February 23, 2024 |publisher=Montverde Academy Athletics}} On January 5, 2023, Queen scored a season-high 34 points and grabbed 11 rebounds in a 66–62 win over fellow national powerhouse Sunrise Christian Academy at the LaPorte Invitational.{{cite news |last=Branham |first=Travis |date=January 6, 2023 |title=NIBC LaPorte Invitational: Derik Queen, Jayden Ross, Gus Yalden and Matas Buzelis standout on day one |url=https://247sports.com/article/nibc-laporte-invitational-derik-queen-jayden-ross-gus-yalden-and-matas-buzelis-standout-on-day-one-202266616/ |access-date=February 23, 2024 |work=[[247Sports]]}} The next day, he posted 24 points and 10 rebounds in a 66–61 victory over [[Wasatch Academy]]. On February 3, 2023, Queen recorded 24 points and 13 rebounds to guide second-ranked Montverde to an 85–48 win over top-ranked Link Academy in a highly anticipated matchup between the two top-ranked teams in the country.{{cite news |last=Divens |first=Jordan |date=February 3, 2023 |title=High school basketball: National Top 10 No. 2 Montverde Academy blows past previously-unbeaten No. 1 Link Academy 84-58 |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/Y5PNgyA7vkCT-QzjCKnIFw/high-school-basketball-national-top-10-no-2-montverde-academy-blows-past-previously-unbeaten-no-1-link-academy-84-58.htm |access-date=February 23, 2024 |work=[[MaxPreps]]}} However, Montverde suffered a 46–45 upset defeat to Sunrise Christian in the quarterfinals of the 2023 GEICO Nationals, which the [[ESPNU]] crew described as "the biggest upset in the 14-year history of the GEICO Nationals."{{cite news |last=Gorches |first=Steve |date=March 30, 2023 |title=Montverde loses to Sunrise in major upset at GEICO High School Nationals |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/2023/03/30/montverde-loses-to-sunrise-in-major-upset-at-geico-high-school-nationals/ |access-date=February 23, 2024 |work=[[Orlando Sentinel]]}} Queen had 10 points and six rebounds in the loss, which ended their season with a record of 23–3. As a junior, he averaged 11.8 points, 6.7 rebounds and 2.2 assists on 61 percent shooting, receiving a [[MaxPreps]] Junior All-American honorable mention.{{cite news |last=Divens |first=Jordan |date=June 14, 2023 |title=High school basketball: Derik Queen moves into top 10 of Class of 2024 after dominant spring |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/k6DlOjcE9EWZ8_3AKHmMlA/high-school-basketball-derik-queen-moves-into-top-10-of-class-of-2024-after-dominant-spring.htm |access-date=February 23, 2024 |work=[[MaxPreps]]}} On November 25, 2023, Queen recorded 24 points and eight rebounds to lead Montverde to a 103–74 win over [[Duncanville High School]].{{cite news |title=Derik Queen's Basketball Stats {{!}} Varsity 23-24 |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/fl/montverde/montverde-academy-eagles/athletes/derik-queen/basketball/stats/?careerid=ts8q2t6671sg0&sportSeasonId=66ece839-d183-4227-9807-2e33d599d076#year=23-24 |access-date=February 23, 2024 |publisher=[[MaxPreps]]}} In their next game, an 86–69 victory over [[IMG Academy]], he posted 25 points and 13 rebounds.{{cite news |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |last2=Biancardi |first2=Paul |author2-link=Paul Biancardi |name-list-style=and |date=February 21, 2024 |title=Top-10 prospect Derik Queen commits to home state Maryland |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/39571528 |access-date=February 23, 2024 |work=[[ESPN]]}} On December 8, Queen tallied 20 points and nine rebounds in a 71–59 win over Link Academy. Queen also played for Team Thill in off-season competitions. In 2023, he led them to an [[Under Armour]] Association (UAA) 17U spring championship after recording 22 points, 15 rebounds and five blocks in their 69–49 title game victory over West Coast Elite.{{cite news|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/k6DlOjcE9EWZ8_3AKHmMlA/high-school-basketball-derik-queen-moves-into-top-10-of-class-of-2024-after-dominant-spring.htm|title=High school basketball: Derik Queen moves into top 10 of Class of 2024 after dominant spring|first=Jordan|last=Divens|work=[[MaxPreps]]|date=June 14, 2023|access-date=February 23, 2024}} ===Recruiting=== Queen was a consensus five-star [[College recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2024 class, according to major recruiting services. On October 27, 2023, he officially narrowed his list of schools down to four finalists: [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]], [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]], [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] and [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston]].{{cite news |last=Tipton |first=Joe |date=October 27, 2023 |title=Top-15 recruit Derik Queen down to 4 schools |url=https://www.on3.com/news/derik-queen-down-to-4-schools-houston-indiana-kansas-maryland/ |access-date=February 23, 2024 |work=On3}} On February 21, 2024, Queen verbally committed to play [[college basketball]] for Maryland. It was one of the first programs to start recruiting Queen, having offered him a scholarship during the summer before his freshman year. {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2024}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Derik Queen | position = [[Center (basketball)|C]] | hometown = [[Montverde, FL]] | highschool = [[Montverde Academy]] (FL) | feet = 6 | inches = 10 | weight = 240 | 40 = | commitdate = Feb 21, 2024 | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 92 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | year = 2025 | 247 overall = 12 | rivals overall = 15 | espn overall = 10 | access-date = February 24, 2024 | bball = yes }} ==College career== Queen enrolled at the [[University of Maryland]] in 2024. Following his freshman season, he was a first-team All-[[Big Ten]] selection by the coaches and won the [[Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year|Big Ten Freshman of the Year]]. In the [[2025 Big Ten men's basketball tournament|2025 Big Ten Tournament]], Queen scored 31 points against the eventual Big Ten champion [[2024–25 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan Wolverines]] in the semifinal. It was the most points ever scored in the tournament by a Maryland freshman and earned him an All-Tournament Team selection.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401743941 |title=Donaldson's court-length drive sends No. 22 Michigan past No. 11 Maryland 81-80 in Big Ten tourney |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=March 15, 2025 |access-date=March 15, 2025}} In the second round of the subsequent [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], Queen scored a fadeaway jump shot at the buzzer to lift Maryland above [[Colorado State Rams men's basketball|Colorado State]], 72-71. It was his first game-winning shot at any level.{{cite news |last1=Henderson |first1=Brady |title=Queen's buzzer shot sends Terrapins to Sweet 16 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/44378618/derik-queen-buzzer-beater-lifts-maryland-sweet-16 |access-date=25 March 2025 |work=ESPN.com |date=24 March 2025 |language=en}} ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== *[https://umterps.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/derik-queen/14091 Maryland Terrapins bio] {{McDonald's All-American Game Boys MVP}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Queen, Derik}} [[Category:2004 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Baltimore]] [[Category:Centers (basketball)]] [[Category:Maryland Terrapins men's basketball players]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]]
